newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: ROKISHKIS PLANS NEW SHARE CAPITAL BOOST.
newsitem.headline: ROKISHKIS PLANS NEW SHARE CAPITAL BOOST.

text.p: Lithuania's Rokishkis Cheese , one of the leading blue chips on the Vilnius bourse, said on Monday that it will propose to its shareholders to increase its share capital in September.

"We are thinking of the possibility to boost our share capital but the decision will be taken by the general shareholders' meeting scheduled for September 12," the director general of the firm, Antanas Trumpa, told Reuters.
"The administration of the company is considering four," Trumpa said but declined to comment on them or provide further details at the moment.
The current share capital of Rokishkis Cheese stands at 30.24 million litas.
The company decided in June to issue 200,000 shares with a face value of ten litas which will be acquired by investment bank Williams De Broe when they are registered with the securities comission.
"According to the agreement (with Williams De Broe) we will be paid no less than 44 litas per share with a face value of ten litas a month after the shares are registered," Trumpa said.
Trumpa added that the securities commission is expected to register the shares before the end of August.

Rokishkis Cheese, one of the three corporates on the elite official list of the Vilnius bourse, posted a 9.47 million litas net profit in the first half of 1997 versus 1.25 million litas net profit in the same period in 1996.
